evidence.summary: The institute is the Ministry of Public Security’s national forensic laboratory (公安部物证鉴定中心, now 公安部鉴定中心). Founded in the early 1970s as the ministry’s 126 Institute, later its Second Research Institute, and established on that basis in 1996, it examines physical evidence and crime scenes for the central authorities and the ministry and re-examines evidence that provincial public security bureaus submit; in 2010 it was named one of China’s ten national-level forensic authentication bodies. The ministry supervises the forensic science journal it publishes.

In June 2020 the US Commerce Department added the institute to the Entity List, finding it implicated in human rights violations and abuses in China’s campaign of repression, mass arbitrary detention, forced labour and high-technology surveillance against Uighurs, Kazakhs and other Muslim minorities in Xinjiang. The department removed it in November 2023 after a removal review.
